title: Soul Snack #66: How Do I Let Go of Anger and Resentment?
excerpt: Are you making choices in love or fear?
bodyHtml:
Are you making choices in love or fear? Take this self-assessment today to find out.


Letting go of anger and resentment is one of the most challenging – and transformative – inner commitments a person can make. In this Soul Snack Linda Francis shares a grounded, compassionate explanation of what it truly takes to release these painful emotions. Rather than offering a quick fix, she describes a lifelong practice: choosing, again and again, not to act on the anger that arises and instead learning to feel it with full awareness. Through this process, listeners discover that emotional healing comes not from suppression, but from conscious choice.

As Linda deepens the teaching, she explains how the universe provides opportunities to challenge the angry and resentful parts of our personalities. These moments – often unexpected – are invitations to grow. 

When anger appears, we can learn to locate it in the body, observe its thoughts, and use our will to refrain from acting from it.

Each time we do this, the frightened parts lose power, and the loving parts gain strength. This is the essence of creating authentic power.

Ultimately, letting go of anger and resentment becomes possible when you choose not to feed these parts of your personality. By feeling the emotion without acting on it, you stop reinforcing it – and you begin cultivating the loving, constructive aspects of yourself that reshape your life.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Snack:

(00:20) — Why letting go begins with commitment
Linda explains why your first step is deciding – fully – that you will no longer allow anger and resentment to run your life. 

(01:06) — How the universe brings growth opportunities
Unexpected situations arise specifically to help you challenge and heal the angry parts of your personality. 

(01:35) — The practice of feeling without acting
You learn how to notice anger’s physical sensations and intense thoughts while using your will to not act from them. 

(02:40) — Why stopping mid-reaction is a breakthrough
Even if you catch yourself in the middle of anger, choosing to feel instead of act is a powerful moment of transformation. 

(03:20) — How loving parts grow stronger as anger loses power
Each time you refrain from acting on resentment, you stop feeding it – allowing the loving parts of your personality to take root. 

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

This week, notice the moments when anger or resentment arise within you. Instead of acting on them, pause. Feel the sensations in your body and witness the thoughts without suppressing or expressing them. Ask yourself: What part of me is feeling this? What would it look like to choose not to act from this place? Each time you commit to feeling rather than reacting, you loosen the grip of the frightened parts and strengthen your ability to create authentically with love.
